newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Germany's Waigel strongly backs Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Germany's Waigel strongly backs Eurofighter.

text.p: The four-nation Eurofighter project received a boost on Thursday as Finance Minister Theo Waigel gave his support, if not an outright promise of funds, for German participation in the venture.

Hoped to provide thousands of jobs in Britain, Germany, France and Italy, Eurofighter has nonetheless been the subject of lengthy political debate and doubts as to whether Europe needs, or can even afford it.

"I want the Eurofighter and consider it necessary both in the national and European interest. Now it's a question of agreeing an acceptable financial model with the manufacturer DASA," Waigel was quoted as saying by the newspaper Die Welt in a summary of an article to appear on Friday.
"I have always fought for Eurofighter," Waigel was further quoted as saying of the project. It is expected to cost Germany alone a total of 23 billion marks ($13.4 billion).
The jet is being jointly developed by Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), British Aerospace, Spain's CASA and Italy's Alenia.

German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said last week after talks with his British counterpart George Robertson that Waigel had pledged to ensure that funds allowing Germany to take part in Eurofighter would be approved following cabinet budget meetings next month.
But Ruehe has also said that German participation was further dependent on funds being redirected into Eurofighter that were initially advanced to DASA for other purposes.
Ruehe had been qouted on Thursday as saying he was confident of Waigel's backing on Eurofighter and that Germany's overall defence budget would not be slashed in the future.

"I have great trust in the promise that (Waigel) gave to the federal armed forces -- 47 billion marks in 1998 and rising thereafter," he was quoted as saying in an advance summary of an interview to be published in Friday's Bild newspaper.

Earlier, he had angrily rejected suggestions by a German Finance Ministry official that defence budgets must be cut as part of a wider austerity drive to help Bonn fill gaping budget gaps and qualify for Europe's single currency.

Referring to comments attributed to Finance Ministry State Secretary Manfred Overhaus on Wednesday, he said that his own contacts on the issue had been with Waigel and Chancellor Helmut Kohl. "A state secretary is not a partner in such discussions," Ruehe told reporters in Bonn.
Ruehe told journalists that in earlier budget talks he had already promised to redirect some of his budget to ensure Germany could be part of Eurofighter.
He said in the Bild interview he would only seek the approval of German parliament for the venture if assured of a full budget and the additional funds from DASA.
He added that any reduction of overall defence funds would moreover jeopardise the ability of the Defence Ministry to carry out its function effectively.

The Defence Ministry budget has come under question from across the political spectrum in recent days. One argument is that Bonn could save billions of marks by reducing, or eradicating entirely, the conscripted part of its 340,000 strong army.
